_comment: SWEG_MELEE_CAGING — coordinated multi-unit melee caging, the faithful counter to the durability wall that the single-point-per-model geometry cannot otherwise express. Two coupled pieces behind one default-off, faction-neutral gate. (1) Charge coordination + wrap placement (Battle._do_charge / _cage_charge_target / _cage_charge_end, code/simulator.py): when a durable enemy brick (Toughness 10+ OR 15+ starting Wounds, the same 'brick' definition simulator.antitank_advance_discipline uses) is within charge reach of two or more melee-capable friendly units in the same Charge phase, their charges are coordinated onto it (instead of the default scatter to crackable chaff) and each charger is placed on the side of the brick farthest from the chargers already on it, so two chargers land ~180 degrees apart (the wrap). (2) Fall-back block (pick_move_intent, code/strategy.py): a caged brick returns HOLD instead of FALL_BACK, so it stays engaged and, as a VEHICLE/MONSTER, shoots only the cage at the Big Guns Never Tire -1 (Battle._do_shoot, which already restricts an in-engagement big gun to targets it is itself engaged with) rather than Falling Back to reposition and re-target freely next turn. The fall-back block half is grounded in the verbatim 10e Fall Back surround rule quoted below; the charge-coordination half is an artificial-intelligence piloting heuristic grounded in the real-play multi-unit-caging pattern (the same class as simulator.staging_discipline), registered here so the auditor tracks it. Default-off, byte-identical off (the gate is the first short-circuit on every path; the per-round Battle._cage_bearings dict is an unused empty dict when the gate is off).

simulator.melee_caging.rule_name: Fall Back (a surrounded unit cannot Fall Back) + Big Guns Never Tire — coordinated multi-unit melee caging counterplay
simulator.melee_caging.quoted_text: each model in that unit can make a Fall Back move by moving a distance in inches less than or equal to its Move characteristic, and when doing so you can move it within Engagement Range of enemy models, provided it does not end that move within Engagement Range of any enemy models - if this is not possible, that unit cannot Fall Back. ... Each time you take a Desperate Escape test for a model, roll one D6. For each roll of 1-2, one model from the unit that is Falling Back is destroyed (selected by you). ... [Big Guns Never Tire] each time a model in a VEHICLE or MONSTER unit makes a ranged attack while its unit is within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units, subtract 1 from that attack's Hit roll, and that attack can only target an enemy unit that its own unit is within Engagement Range of.
simulator.melee_caging.trigger: SWEG_MELEE_CAGING=1 (default-off; unset or '0' is the byte-identical kill-switch). Fall-back-block half: the acting unit (in code/strategy.py pick_move_intent) is a durable brick (Toughness 10 or higher, or 15 or more starting Wounds), is within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units, and is wrapped on OPPOSING SIDES - within Engagement Range of two or more enemy units whose bearings from it differ by at least 120 degrees. Charge-coordination half: in Battle._do_charge, a charger that already wants to charge and already has a live pick_charge_target is redirected onto a durable brick that is within its 1"-12" base-edge declaration range AND within the same declaration range of at least two melee-capable friendly units (including the charger).
simulator.melee_caging.effect: ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC composed with a verbatim core rule; not a novel rules claim. Fall-back block: a caged brick returns HOLD instead of FALL_BACK - it cannot Fall Back per the quoted surround rule ('if this is not possible, that unit cannot Fall Back'), so it stays engaged and, being a VEHICLE or MONSTER, shoots only the cage at the Big Guns Never Tire -1 (already modelled in Battle._do_shoot). Caging does not silence the platform; it forces it to fight the cage instead of re-targeting freely and blocks the free fall-back-reposition that is the durables' UPTIME win channel (the ranged-hold kill-switch counterfactual moved Chaos Knights 87.5 -> 65.0 by removing exactly this uptime). Charge coordination: friendly melee mass converges its already-committed charges onto one brick and wraps it (each charger placed on the side farthest from the chargers already on it) instead of trickling one unit per round onto the brick while the rest scatter to crackable chaff - the coordinated wrap real players use and the sim's per-activation charge picker does not. GEOMETRIC APPROXIMATION (see 'approximation'): SwegHammer represents each model as a single point, so it cannot express a literal closed ring of models around a base, which is what makes a real wrap deny every fall-back exit. The point geometry's closest faithful proxy is opposing-sides engagement (two or more Engagement-Range enemies whose bearings differ by at least 120 degrees); a single cage member never blocks Fall Back, preserving the rule that an un-surrounded unit may always Fall Back. We do not claim a geometric proof of no-escape - a point can in principle slip between two points - we model the tactical outcome the wrap produces. Deterministic: the wrap placement is a fixed 10-degree candidate ring with a deterministic tie-break, drawing no random numbers, so the gate-on arm consumes no extra RNG and the gate-off arm is byte-identical (the caging path is the first short-circuit on _do_charge and pick_move_intent, and the per-round Battle._cage_bearings dict is never written when the gate is off).
